title: The Cellar of Cold Spring
premise: Wren Underhill takes a teaching post at Cold Spring Academy, where students vanish one by one and the town's founders left behind a sealed cellar door that an excavation crew finally breaks open. Wren discovers the disappearances feed a ritual of renewal that the founders' descendants have maintained for generations, and that the school's beloved headmistress intends to complete it with Wren as the final offering. To save the remaining students, Wren must finish the ritual differently — unbinding it rather than feeding it — a choice that costs them their memories of the past seven years but frees the trapped children and dissolves the school's power forever.
about_author: Xanthe Vane is the pen name of a former boarding-school teacher who spent a decade collecting the strange, half-whispered histories of old New England institutions. They write horror about places that remember more than the people inside them.

chapters.title: First Bell
chapters.summary: Wren arrives at Cold Spring Academy in late autumn, unsettled by the staff's practiced warmth and the empty desks no one explains. A student named Ilsa mentions 'the ones who went home early.' POV: Wren. Emotional beat: cautious hope curdling into quiet unease.

chapters.title: The Attendance Book
chapters.summary: Wren finds decades of attendance records with names struck through in red ink, always in threes, always near solstices. The headmistress, Odile Marsh, gently warns them not to pry. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the thrill of investigation shadowed by institutional menace.

chapters.title: What the Ground Gives Back
chapters.summary: An excavation crew on the north lawn unearths an iron door — scratched, dented, sealed from the inside. That night Wren hears dragging sounds beneath the floorboards and, for the first time, answers them. POV: Wren, with a brief interlude from Ilsa's diary. Emotional beat: dread becoming undeniable.

chapters.title: Sealed From Within
chapters.summary: Wren researches the school's four founders and learns the door was locked during the founding winter, when three children died. In the cellar's antechamber they find chalk circles still warm. Odile catches them there — and instead of punishing them, thanks them. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the sickening realization they were meant to find this.

chapters.title: The Chosen Substitute
chapters.summary: Odile reveals the ritual: every generation, an outsider must 'complete the founders' work' or the school fails and the town starves. Wren is this cycle's chosen vessel. Their protests are met with kindness, which is worse. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: betrayal and claustrophobic entrapment.

chapters.title: Found
chapters.summary: Wren escapes to the village and finds Ilsa hiding in the chapel attic; together they uncover the descendants' ledger showing the 'missing' students are alive below, sustained as anchors for the ritual. POV: alternating Wren and Ilsa. Emotional beat: the fragile spark of found family and shared resolve.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: The staff seal the campus. Wren and Ilsa descend through the broken door into the cellar city where the taken children wait, hollow-eyed, tended by something wearing the founders' faces. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: terror tempered by tenderness toward the lost kids.

chapters.title: The Founders' Work
chapters.summary: Odile begins the rite at the heart-chamber altar, binding Wren's identity into the circle — their name, their seven years of self-told explanations peeling away. Wren understands the ritual can be turned: finished, but inverted. POV: Wren, fragmenting. Emotional beat: climax — selfhood offered up as the price.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: With Ilsa speaking their true name back to them, Wren completes the ritual in reverse, releasing the anchors and collapsing the founders' power. The thing beneath screams itself into silence; Odile crumbles to dust mid-benediction. POV: Wren and Ilsa. Emotional beat: cathartic sacrifice and release.

chapters.title: Cold Spring, Thawing
chapters.summary: The children wake with no memory of the cellar; the school closes quietly. Wren remembers nothing before the excavation — but keeps a red-inked attendance book annotated in their own hand: everyone accounted for. Ilsa calls them family anyway. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — identity traded for others' freedom, love persisting without memory.
